findings.diagnosis: The prompt routinely ranks cuts too high when they separate a finite verb/coproduct/auxiliary from the words that complete its core argument, producing orphaned predicates or scope flips.
findings.evidence: en_us_44,en_us_1650,en_us_375,en_us_419,en_us_1060,en_us_292,en_us_1617,en_us_1062,en_us_1081,en_us_101 — each kept a cut that leaves a verb, copula, or auxiliary standing without its immediately following essential complement (prepositional/location/time phrase, measurement, or clausal/object), which the target fixes by keeping the verb+complement together.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences where a finite verb, copula, or auxiliary is immediately followed (within the next few tokens) by a prepositional phrase, temporal expression, measurement/unit, named location, or clausal/direct-object phrase that supplies the verb's core complement.

edit.text: Do not cut immediately after a finite verb/copula/auxiliary when the following words form its essential complement (object, prepositional phrase of place/time/measurement, or clausal complement).
